name: Erasing the Invisible
description: The task evaluates the robustness of invisible watermarking techniques embedded in AI-generated images against adversarial attacks. Participants must design methods to remove or degrade watermarks while preserving the visual quality of the images.

cr:input.name: ETI_Competition_Data
cr:input.description: A dataset of 300 AI-generated images per track (Beige-box and Black-box) embedded with invisible watermarks using various techniques. Features include `image_index` and `watermarked_image`. Example techniques: Gaussian Shading, StegaStamp, JigMark, PRC, StableSignature, Trufo.

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: A set of 300 attacked images in PNG format, corresponding to the input images. The goal is to reduce watermark detection scores (A) while minimizing image quality degradation (Q).

field.name: attacked_image
field.description: The attacked image in PNG format, corresponding to the input watermarked image.

cr:evaluation.primaryMetric: Final Score (Euclidean distance in Q-A space)
metrics: Final Score (Euclidean distance in Q-A space)
Image Quality Degradation (Q) - weighted aggregation of 8 IQMs
cr:evaluation.notes: The final score is computed as the Euclidean distance in Q-A space: sqrt(Q^2 + A^2). Detection thresholds for A are pre-calibrated using 10,000 unwatermarked images per watermark type. Q aggregates eight IQMs (PSNR, SSIM, NMI, FID, CLIP-FID, LPIPS, ∆Aesthetics, ∆Artifacts) using a weighted formula.

open_questions: Are participants allowed to use external data for training or fine-tuning their models?

Are there any specific preprocessing steps required for the input images beyond what is described in the evaluation pipeline?
